one_liner: Rust research malloc (elfmalloc) with a C API, faster than glibc ptmalloc2 and often 2017 jemalloc on multithreaded benchmarks.
what_it_does: elfmalloc is a general-purpose multithreaded allocator written in Rust that exposes both a Rust Alloc implementation and the C malloc/free API. The elfc crate builds it as a cdylib (.so) that replaces malloc in existing C and C++ programs through LD_PRELOAD or dlopen; there is no header or link-time C++ integration. The repository also holds a Bonwick-style object slab allocator (slab-alloc), a bootstrapping allocator, an mmap wrapper and the bagpipe concurrent bag used inside elfmalloc.
how_it_is_fast: Size-class slabs ('Slags') with a bit-set of free objects; the claimed bit and the free count share one word so remote frees are a single fetch-or plus fetch-add with no retry loop. A per-thread, per-size-class fixed-size stack (MagazineCache front end, after Bonwick's magazines) serves most allocations and frees without atomics and batches remote frees by composing masks before the fetch-or. Global pools are bagpipes (weakly ordered concurrent bags) instead of locked lists, and free() finds an object's path by rounding the pointer down to a 2 MiB-aligned header, following scalloc's virtual-span idea.
when_to_use: Research or comparison runs on 64-bit Linux where you want a scalloc-style allocator with a different global-structure design to test against.
Multithreaded C or C++ programs dominated by small-object churn or producer-consumer frees, where the authors' plots show it ahead of ptmalloc2 and usually ahead of 2017 jemalloc.
Rust projects that need a type-specific object allocator (slab-alloc, object-alloc traits) and can build with an old nightly toolchain.
Throughput matters more than resident memory and the process is long-running with stable allocation patterns.
when_not_to_use: Production use: the README calls elfmalloc 'early alpha' with 'certainly undiscovered bugs', and the project has been unmaintained since 2020.

Memory-constrained services: dirty pages are never returned to the OS (the design doc says there is no madvise reclamation), and threadtest and producer-consumer show clearly higher memory use than the competitors.
macOS, Windows or 32-bit targets: Mac 'will currently encounter bugs or crashes', 32-bit support is untested, and Windows CI was never fixed (issue #133).
Anyone needing a modern drop-in: mimalloc, snmalloc and current jemalloc/tcmalloc were never compared, so the 2017 lead may not hold.

integration.form: crate (elfmalloc) plus a cdylib shared lib (elfc) for LD_PRELOAD
integration.dependencies: Sibling path crates (alloc-fmt, alloc-tls, bagpipe, bsalloc, malloc-bind, mmap-alloc) plus lazy_static, libc, log 0.3, num_cpus, smallvec 0.4, sysconf
integration.min_toolchain: Rust nightly from about 2018 (uses feature gates allocator_api, const_fn, const_size_of, thread_local_state, core_intrinsics); exact pinned nightly not documented
integration.platforms: 64-bit Linux (relatively complete); macOS crashes; 32-bit untested; Windows not working in CI
integration.thread_safety: Thread-safe; designed for multithreaded allocation with cross-thread (remote) frees
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial: replaces glibc malloc via LD_PRELOAD of the elfc .so, but has to be built with an old nightly Rust and is alpha quality

gotchas: lib.rs relies on nightly feature gates that have since been removed or renamed (const_size_of, the old Alloc trait), so a current nightly is unlikely to build it without patches.
When the crate is linked into a Rust program without the use_default_allocator feature, bsalloc becomes the global heap and the README warns that other allocations get slower.
The c-api feature, which elfc enables, speeds up the C API at the cost of worse memory use for the Rust Alloc API.
It reserves a very large (many-terabyte) virtual region up front in 2 MiB pages, which can trip overcommit limits, ulimit -v or sanitizers.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Mesh targets memory compaction and IsoAlloc targets hardening; pick elfmalloc only to study or benchmark a lock-free, scalloc-like Rust design that can be preloaded into C programs. For production C++ allocator replacement, a maintained sibling such as Mesh, or mimalloc outside this list, is the safer choice.
verified_claims_summary: The authors LD_PRELOADed elfmalloc into scalloc-artifact threadtest and shbench (objects of 64 B or less, and objects of a few KB) and into an adapted rpmalloc-benchmark producer-consumer run at 1-32 threads on dual Xeon E5-2620v4 under WSL, comparing against glibc 2.19 ptmalloc2, an August 2017 jemalloc dev build, llalloc and rpmalloc. The plots are normalised to ptmalloc2 and show elfmalloc leading most configurations, with jemalloc ahead at 32 threads on small-object threadtest and llalloc ahead on shbench at low thread counts. No compiler flags or numeric ratios are given, and the page is marked work in progress.
status_note: Abandoned since 2020 (alpha, 2018-era nightly Rust); Apache-2.0/MIT, so it is free to copy, but it is research code to read and benchmark rather than to ship.
